1.15 Rust and OCaml extraction pools

metadata-extract WORKERS reads a JSON array of UTF-8 paths from stdin. The OCaml equivalent metadata-extract-oxcaml WORKERS reads NUL-delimited paths. Both emit ExifTool JSON records in input order without deserializing and reserializing their metadata values in the native worker.

Both launch one ExifTool process per path with the same extraction flags and allow 1–36 workers. Rust schedules them through threads; OCaml multiplexes stdout/stderr pipes from child processes. The expensive metadata parser remains ExifTool in both cases. Rust or OCaml execution does not make its metadata a DNG pixel digest.

To select a pool for the portable snapshot:

DNG_METADATA_BACKEND="$PWD/rust-scanner/target/release/metadata-extract" \
DNG_METADATA_WORKERS=4 \
uv run python portable_metadata.py /media/source/foto /media/reference/foto \
  archives/source --batch-size 16

The OCaml route uses DNG_METADATA_BACKEND="$PWD/metadata-extract-oxcaml". DNG_METADATA_PREFETCH_BATCHES defaults to four when a native pool is selected and accepts 1–16. DNG_METADATA_SHARDS can run independent extraction/compression shards, with the total native worker budget apportioned across them. A separate index owner receives bounded atomic batches. Shard count must not exceed the worker budget or 16. Only the coordinator writes its checkpoint; workers do not compete for the same SQLite connection.
